info.title: WIP Document Store Service
info.description:
## World In a Pie - Document Storage and Validation

The Document Store service manages documents that conform to templates defined in the Template Store.

### Key Features

- **Document Storage**: Store and retrieve documents with template validation
- **Template Validation**: Validate documents against template schemas
- **Versioning**: Automatic document versioning with identity-based upsert
- **Identity Management**: SHA-256 identity hash based on template identity fields
- **Terminology Validation**: Validate term fields against Def-Store terminologies

### Document Lifecycle

1. Submit document with template_id and data
2. Fetch template from Template Store (with inheritance resolved)
3. Validate data against template fields and rules
4. Compute identity hash from identity fields
5. Create new document or new version if identity exists

### Authentication

All endpoints require API key authentication via the `X-API-Key` header.

### Integration

- **Registry Service**: Documents get unique IDs (UUID7)
- **Template Store Service**: Fetch templates for validation
- **Def-Store Service**: Validate term field values

Each document is validated against the specified template before creation.
For single items, uses direct creation. For multiple items, uses optimized
batch operations with cache warmup.

patch.description:
Apply JSON Merge Patches (RFC 7396) to one or more existing documents.

Each item is processed independently and a new document version is created
on success. Errors are returned per item in the BulkResponse — the endpoint
always returns HTTP 200, matching the bulk-first contract.

Merge semantics:
- Objects at the same path are deep-merged
- Arrays are replaced (send the full array)
- A null value deletes the field

Constraints:
- Identity fields cannot be changed (use POST to create a new document)
- Namespace cannot be changed (PATCH modifies `data`, and `metadata.custom` via `metadata_patch`)
- A soft-deleted document is `not_found`; re-post its full data to bring it back
- Optional per-item `if_match` provides optimistic concurrency control: pass the
  document's `revision` (equal to `version`, except on a `versioned: false`
  template, where each in-place write moves it on)

After merge the full document is re-validated against the same template
version recorded on the existing document, term and file references are
re-resolved, and a new version is written. Reporting-sync sees the same
DOCUMENT_UPDATED event as POST-driven version bumps.

A hard delete is refused (error_code=invalid_state, details.rule=referenced) while other documents still reference it; details.referrers groups them by namespace and template. post.summary: Migrate documents to a newer template version
post.description:
Re-pin every active document currently on `from_version` to `to_version`
The "move" half of the template-version lifecycle.

Each document's existing data is re-validated against the TARGET version
(which must be active; the source may be inactive/frozen). On apply a new
document version is created — or the single version is overwritten in place
for `versioned: false` templates — pinned to `to_version`, keeping the same
`document_id` and `identity_hash`. No data transformation happens here, except
field renames declared on the target template version, which mechanically re-key
each document's data to the new field names.

Identity-preserving only: the two template versions must declare the same
`identity_fields`, otherwise the re-pin would change the identity hash — that
is a fork (create new documents), not a migrate, and the whole operation is
rejected with `identity_fields_changed`.

Workflow: run with `dry_run=true` (default) for a per-document readiness
report — a result with `failed==0` guarantees a successful apply (barring
concurrent writes). Fix any failing documents (e.g. PATCH-null a removed
field) while the source version is still writable, optionally freeze the
source version (deactivate) as a migration lock, then re-run with
`dry_run=false`.

Bulk-first: always HTTP 200, per-document outcome in the `results` array.
Operation-level problems (bad versions, identity mismatch, inactive target)
return a 4xx.

Grouped from the namespace's documents, not from template ownership: a
document's namespace is independent of its template's namespace, so listing
the templates a namespace owns cannot answer this — a namespace whose

post.description:
Validate document data against a template without saving.

This is useful for:
- Pre-validation before submission
- Testing document data against templates
- Computing identity hash

Returns validation result with:
- valid: Whether the document passes validation
- errors: List of validation errors
- warnings: Non-blocking warnings
- identity_hash: Computed identity hash (if valid)
- template_version: Template version used

post.summary: Validate multiple documents against one template without saving
post.description:
Validate a batch of documents against a single template, without saving.

Bulk, side-effect-free counterpart to `/validate` — the dry-run validator that
finally got the array form the rest of the write surface already has. All items
validate against ONE `template_id` in ONE `namespace`; the template (and its
nested term/template references) is warmed into cache once, then each item is
validated from cache.

Returns `{ results: [...] }` — one `ValidationResponse` per input item, in the
same order. A document being invalid is reported by that item's `valid: false`
+ `errors` (not as a batch error). An unresolvable `template_id` fails the whole
request with 404, since the batch is single-template.

Zero persistence: no documents created, no versions, no identity-hash registry
side effects (identity hashes are computed locally).

post.summary: Validate documents against an inline candidate template definition
post.description:
The what-if dry-run for schema evolution: "would my documents still validate
against this draft next version?" — answered before the version exists.

The candidate definition is used inline: nothing is created, cached, or
registered, and no draft version pollutes the template's version catalog.
Provide either explicit `documents` payloads, or `sample_template_id` to run
the candidate against the most recently updated active documents of an
existing template (`sample_limit`, default 100, max 500).

Reference values inside the candidate (terminology_ref etc.) should be
canonical IDs or resolvable synonyms — an unresolvable reference surfaces as
a per-document validation error, exactly as it would on a real write.

Declared renames are honored: a candidate carrying `renames`
(`{new_field: old_field}`) validates each document as-if re-keyed — the
same semantics an applied migration uses — so a declared rename does not
false-fail as an unknown old field plus a missing new one.

get.summary: Get flattened table view of documents
get.description:
Get documents for a template in a flattened table format.

This endpoint treats the template as a database table, returning documents as rows.
Array fields can be flattened into multiple rows (cross-product) or kept as JSON.

**Array Handling:**
- 0 arrays: 1 row per document
- 1 array: Flatten into multiple rows
- 2+ arrays, cross-product ≤ max_cross_product rows (default 1000, tunable up to 10000): Cross-product (flatten all)
- 2+ arrays, cross-product > max_cross_product rows: Keep arrays as JSON fields

**Metadata Columns:**
All rows include system columns prefixed with underscore:
- `_document_id`: Document ID
- `_version`: Document version
- `_identity_hash`: Identity hash
- `_status`: Document status
- `_created_at`: Creation timestamp
- `_updated_at`: Last update timestamp

**Access:** the caller needs read on the namespace the template lives in —
the table's columns are the template's full declared layout (inherited
fields included), and a template's schema is shown only to readers of its
namespace, as the template store's own reads do. Without it the answer is
404, even when the caller can read documents on the template in another
namespace; read those through `GET /documents?template_id=…&namespace=…`.
The rows are then limited to the namespaces the caller can read.

schema.description: Only documents in this namespace, which is also where a bare template value is resolved (a shared template: wip:PATIENT or its id). Without it, the documents of every namespace the caller can read.

post.description:
Upload a file to storage.

The file receives a unique ID from the Registry and is stored in the object store.
Initially the file has status 'orphan' until it's referenced by a document.

Metadata can be provided as form fields:
- description: Human-readable description
- tags: Comma-separated tags (e.g., "invoice,2024,important")
- category: Classification category
- custom: A JSON object of custom metadata fields (e.g. {"source": "scanner"})
- allowed_templates: Comma-separated templates whose documents may use this file. Each names a
  template (value, NS:VALUE, id or synonym) and is stored as its canonical id; one that names no
  template is refused (400).

post.description:
Bring soft-deleted files back without re-uploading them. A soft-deleted file is
retired, not gone: its record and its bytes are kept, and this returns it to
service under the same file_id.

Per item:
- `reactivated` — the file was inactive and is live again: `orphan`, or `active`
  when documents still reference it (a file deleted with force=true keeps its
  reference count).
- `unchanged` — the file was not inactive.
- error `not_found` — no such file, or one in a namespace the caller cannot read.
- error `forbidden` — the caller can read the file's namespace but not write it.
- error `invalid_state`, details.rule `storage_missing` — the object store no
  longer holds the file's bytes. Upload the same bytes again: an upload of a
  soft-deleted file's bytes revives it too, under the same file_id.

Find all active documents that reference a specific file.

post.summary: Delete the stored objects of a namespace being deleted
post.description:
Remove objects from file storage on behalf of namespace deletion. The
Registry's deletion journal records each file's storage key before any
metadata is removed and sends those keys here, so the step can be retried
even after the files' records are gone.

Guards, because this removes bytes outright:
- wip-admins / wip-services only;
- the Registry must hold a deletion journal for the namespace that is
  still running (`in_progress`, `failed` or `completed_with_warnings`, the
  states a deletion resumes from), and the namespace must not be live —
  without such a journal, or for a live namespace, the request is refused
  with 409, and with an unreachable Registry with 503. A namespace that is
  gone, locked, or not visible to this service's key is never by itself a
  reason to delete bytes;
- a key whose file record belongs to a different namespace is refused
  per key and left untouched.

Deleting an object that does not exist counts as deleted, so a retried
request is safe. Always 200 once the guards pass: per-key outcomes are in
`deleted`, `refused` and `failed`.

post.description:
Import documents from a CSV/XLSX file.

Upload a file with a column mapping to create documents in bulk.
Use the /preview endpoint first to see the file structure.

The column_mapping maps CSV column names to template field names:
{"CSV Column Name": "template_field_name", ...}

Term fields: use human-readable values in the CSV (e.g., "United Kingdom").
WIP resolves them to term_ids automatically.

Cells are converted to their field's type before validation: number and
integer fields take numerals, boolean fields true/false, yes/no or 1/0
(any case), date fields YYYY-MM-DD (an XLSX date cell works as is),
datetime fields ISO 8601. A cell that cannot be read as its field's type
fails its row, reported in ``errors`` like a validation failure.

Every row is attempted and reported (``skip_errors`` true, the default)
unless ``skip_errors`` is false. ``results`` lists at most the first 100
created rows and ``errors`` the first 50 failed ones; ``results_truncated``
and ``errors_truncated`` say when a list was cut, and ``succeeded`` /
``failed`` always count every row.

Kick off a backup of one or more namespaces.

The URL ``{namespace}`` is the anchor. ``all_namespaces`` backs up every
registry namespace; ``namespaces`` adds an explicit set alongside the
anchor. Admin permission is required on every namespace in the resolved set.

post.summary: Restore a namespace from an uploaded archive
post.description:
Upload an archive and restore it.

Admin is asked on ``target_namespace``, or on the URL ``namespace`` when
none is given; a ``restore`` or ``merge`` also needs admin on every
namespace the archive carries, and a ``fresh`` restore given only a
``namespace_map`` needs admin on the map's targets alone (the URL
``namespace`` then gates nothing). The URL ``namespace`` is not the
destination. The destination is the archive's own namespace(s): a plain ``restore`` writes
each one to itself and refuses a ``target_namespace`` that differs; a
``merge`` of a single-namespace archive may be redirected with
``target_namespace``; a ``fresh`` restore needs ``target_namespace`` or
``namespace_map``. An explicit target is honoured or refused, never
replaced.

The archive is streamed to disk at ``$WIP_BACKUP_DIR/{job_id}.zip`` so
multi-GB uploads don't buffer in RAM.

post.summary: Verify a namespace's referential, identity and mandatory-field integrity
post.description:
Check that a namespace's data is internally consistent.

Every reference resolves — template, term, document, file — every
document's stored identity hash still matches its own content, and each
document's current version has a value for every field its pinned
template version declares mandatory (nested objects and array items
against their own pinned versions). This is the
referential twin of reporting-sync's parity check: that one compares
MongoDB against PostgreSQL, this one compares MongoDB against itself.

It matters most after a restore, which writes with `insert_many` and
validates nothing (deliberately — per-record validation while writing
would undo the bulk write path that makes restore fast). A restore starts
one of these per restored namespace automatically and records the job ids
on its own record; this endpoint is the same check on demand.

Findings do not fail the job. The check ran and its answer is the
deliverable: the job completes, `result.status` is healthy / warning /
error / incomplete (a check could not run because a store did not
answer), and `result.issues` carries a capped sample.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream of job progress
get.description:
SSE stream of :class:`BackupProgressMessage` envelopes for a job.

Wire format
-----------
The ``data:`` payload of every ``progress`` event is a JSON-encoded
:class:`BackupProgressMessage` (see ``models/backup_job.py``). **This is
not ``wip_archive.models.ProgressEvent``** — that type is an
implementation detail and must not be exposed on the wire (Guardrail 2).

Stream the archive a job retains, wherever it lives.

Backup jobs serve their output: COMPLETE status required (an incomplete
backup has no valid archive), and read suffices, on EVERY namespace the
backup covers: the archive holds each one's data.
Restore jobs serve their INPUT: it is fully on disk before the job even
starts, so it is valid regardless of the job's outcome — a FAILED
restore's input is the most useful one to re-download. It carries the
archive's own namespaces' data, so admin is required on every namespace
the job writes and every one the archive holds (_check_job_permission);
a fresh restore's input, whose sources may not exist here, only to the
key that created the job or a platform admin.

post.summary: Restore from an existing job's retained archive
post.description:
Re-run a restore (or restore a backup you already made) without
re-uploading the archive — the bytes are already retained server-side.

The new restore job receives its OWN archive copy (a server-side object
copy in the bucket, or a plain scratch copy with its own age), so deleting either job
never removes the archive out from under the other. Authorization is
two-layered: admin on every namespace the SOURCE job spans (reading the
archive is download-equivalent), then the same per-namespace admin
checks the upload restore runs, over the namespaces the restore will
write (the manifest's list, or the zip's namespaces/ tree when the
manifest lists none).

Re-hash referent-identity documents to the resolved-referent feed.

Term/reference-typed identity fields hash their resolved referent's
canonical ID; documents written before that rule carry spelling-fed
hashes. This pass recomputes each document's hash from its stored
resolutions, updates every version row, and re-keys the Registry's
composite-key claims. Dry-run (the default) only reports — read it
first: collision groups are formerly-forked documents now converging
on one identity, which need vocabulary curation and are never
applied. An apply is safe to re-run: it re-sends the Registry re-key for
documents whose stored hash is already right, so a run whose Registry leg
failed converges; read registry_failed, not only applied. Reporting re-syncs via replay afterwards; the response says so.

Requires admin permission on the namespace.

Release the Registry synonyms of retired documents.

A soft-deleted document's synonyms — its identity-values synonym and any
caller-added ones — are released: they stay recorded on its Registry entry
but neither block a different identity with the same spellings nor
resolve. Its canonical ID and identity keep resolving, so re-posting it
still revives it. Deletes and revivals do this as they happen; this pass
covers documents retired before that, and any delete whose Registry call
failed. With revive=true it also reclaims the synonyms of active
documents (a revival whose Registry call failed). Dry-run (the default)
only reports. Idempotent.

Requires admin permission on the namespace.

get.description: Root endpoint with service information.

Health check endpoint.

Verifies MongoDB, Registry, Template Store, and Def-Store connectivity.
`status`, though, reports this service's own storage (MongoDB) and nothing
else: a peer that cannot be reached is named in its own key (`registry`,
`template_store`, `def_store`, `file_storage`, and the event bus in
`nats`) while `status` stays
`healthy` and the answer stays 200. Only MongoDB failing sets `unhealthy`,
which answers 503 with the same body — a probe reading only the status code
(the image's HEALTHCHECK, curl -f) must not see 200. Orchestrators probe
/ready and /livez instead.

Peers stay out of `status` deliberately: services start in parallel with no
ordering gate, each carrying its own startup retry, so a status that
followed peers would have to converge along registry -> template-store ->
document-store and would re-serialise cold boot; /livez does no I/O because
restarting a process cannot restore a dependency. Read the per-dependency
keys for peer state — a store whose Registry is unreachable still refuses
writes at the request layer, so `status: healthy` means "my storage is up",
not "every request will succeed".

Uncached health for callers that read the dependency keys: a live probe,
not the 30s cached fan-out root /health serves by default (root
/health?fresh=true probes live too).

NATS event-bus state and counters: published, queued for retry, and
dropped (by reason). Dropped events are missing from reporting until a
batch sync repairs them. Operator-only: its last error can name a
subject, and subjects carry namespaces and entity IDs.

Readiness check endpoint.

Returns 200 when the service is ready to accept traffic.

Get timing statistics for document creation and validation.

Returns aggregated timing for:

**Creation stages:**
- 1_validation: Full validation pipeline
- 2_find_existing: MongoDB query for existing identity
- 3_create_new: Create new document (includes 3a + 3b)
- 3a_registry_id: Registry HTTP call for document ID
- 3b_mongo_insert: MongoDB insert
- total: End-to-end creation time

**Validation stages:**
- 1_structural: Basic dict validation
- 2_template_resolution: Fetch template (cached)
- 3_field_validation: Field type and constraint checking
- 4_term_validation: Term validation (local with cached terminologies)
- 5_rule_evaluation: Cross-field rule checking
- 6_identity_computation: Identity hash computation

post.description: Reset all timing statistics (creation and validation).

get.description:
Get cache statistics for the Template Store client, and Def-Store's
term-resolution counters.

- Template cache: pinned versions kept, "latest" for a few seconds
- Def-Store: nothing is cached; terms and terminologies are asked of
  Def-Store on every write

post.description: Clear all caches (template and term validation).

get.description:
Check the referential, identity and mandatory-field integrity of documents.

Scans documents for:
- Template, term, document and file references that do not resolve, and
  references to an inactive template version
- Stored identity hashes that no longer match the document's data
- Mandatory fields of the pinned template version with no value in a
  document's current version (nested objects and array items against
  their own pinned versions)

Args:
    status: Filter documents by status ('active', 'inactive')
    template_id: Filter documents by template_id
    limit: Maximum number of documents to check (0 = all, default: all)
    check_term_refs: Whether to check term references (default true, can be slow)
    recent_first: Check most recently created documents first (default false)

Returns:
    IntegrityCheckResult with status, summary, and list of issues

BackupJobKind.title: BackupJobKind
BackupJobKind.description: What long-running operation this job is running.

source_namespaces.title: Source Namespaces
source_namespaces.description: An uploaded restore or merge: the archive's own namespaces, whose data its retained input carries (see BackupJob)

BackupJobSnapshot.title: BackupJobSnapshot
BackupJobSnapshot.description: API response shape for a BackupJob — hides mongo _id and trims internals.

BackupJobStatus.title: BackupJobStatus
BackupJobStatus.description: Lifecycle status for a backup/restore job.

namespaces.title: Namespaces
namespaces.description: Also back up these namespaces into the same archive (joined with the URL's {namespace}). Omit for single-namespace.

all_namespaces.title: All Namespaces
all_namespaces.description: Back up EVERY namespace the registry lists (incl. 'wip') into one archive. Overrides `namespaces`/{namespace}.

include_files.title: Include Files
include_files.description: Include file blobs in the archive

include_inactive.title: Include Inactive
include_inactive.description: Retired parameter — rejected with 400 if set. Its filter matched a status no persisted entity carries, so it never excluded anything. Backups carry every entity in every status; the one exception is inactive template versions nothing in the archive needs (see include_inactive_templates).

include_inactive_templates.title: Include Inactive Templates
include_inactive_templates.description: Keep every inactive template version. By default a backup leaves out the inactive versions nothing in the archive needs: it carries every version that is not inactive (drafts included), every inactive version an exported document is pinned to or a carried version extends or pins as a nested template, and the highest version of a template whose versions are all inactive.

skip_closure.title: Skip Closure
skip_closure.description: Retired toolkit-export parameter — rejected with 400 if set. The direct engine always includes term relations.

skip_synonyms.title: Skip Synonyms
skip_synonyms.description: Retired toolkit-export parameter — rejected with 400 if set. Synonyms travel inside registry entries.

latest_only.title: Latest Only
latest_only.description: Retired toolkit-export parameter — rejected with 400 if set. The direct engine exports every version; when this flag was silently ignored it also mis-stamped the manifest as latest-only.

template_prefixes.title: Template Prefixes
template_prefixes.description: Retired toolkit-export parameter — rejected with 400 if set. The direct engine has no template filter.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: Retired toolkit-export parameter — rejected with 400 if set. (Restore, by contrast, supports a real dry run.)

BackupRequest.title: BackupRequest
BackupRequest.description:
Request body for POST /backup/namespaces/{namespace}/backup.

Most fields map to keyword arguments of the underlying backup engine; the
factory in ``backup_service`` forwards this dict as ``options``. The
multi-namespace selectors (`namespaces`, `all_namespaces`) are resolved in
the endpoint, not forwarded to the engine.

file.title: File
file.description: CSV or XLSX file to import

column_mapping.title: Column Mapping
column_mapping.description: JSON object mapping CSV columns to template fields, e.g. {"Name": "name", "Email": "email"}

skip_errors.title: Skip Errors
skip_errors.description: Report a row that fails and go on with the next (the default); false stops at the first failing row and reports the rest skipped

file.title: File
file.description: CSV or XLSX file to preview

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: 'restore' requires an empty target and inserts everything, preserving every id. 'merge' takes the archive as a delta against an existing, possibly non-empty namespace, preserving ids and resolving what the target already holds by the on_clash policy. 'fresh' keeps nothing: every entity is registered anew with a Registry-minted id and every reference is rewritten, which is what lets a namespace be restored beside the one it came from.

target_namespace.title: Target Namespace
target_namespace.description: Where to write. Honoured or refused, never ignored: a plain 'restore' writes each archived namespace to itself and refuses a different target (an id-preserving restore cannot re-namespace data); a 'merge' of a single-namespace archive writes into this namespace; a 'fresh' restore requires this or namespace_map, since it places new identities. A multi-namespace archive takes no target in restore or merge mode.

namespace_map.title: Namespace Map
namespace_map.description: Fresh only — JSON object mapping EVERY archived namespace to its target, e.g. {"ns-a": "copy-a", "ns-b": "copy-a"}. Required for multi-namespace archives (there is no implicit default: an unmapped namespace restored to its old name would collide with the live original). Several sources may share one target; Registry-key collisions between them refuse at plan time. A target may equal its source name only when that namespace is empty or absent.

on_clash.title: On Clash
on_clash.description: Merge only — what to do when the target already holds a document's identity. 'skip' (default) keeps the target's version; 'overwrite' appends the archive's latest version on top of the target's head, preserving both histories; 'newer' does the same but only where the archive's copy was updated more recently, keeping the target's on a tie.

older_versions.title: Older Versions
older_versions.description: Merge only — when 'overwrite' or 'newer' appends the archive's version on top of the target's, what happens to the target's older versions. 'retire' (default) soft-deletes them, as a normal write does; 'keep' leaves them active, so the document has several active versions.

add_missing.title: Add Missing
add_missing.description: Merge only — insert terminologies and templates the target does not have. Without it, a definition the target lacks refuses the merge: changing a live namespace's definitions is an active decision, never a side effect of restoring data into it.

extend_terminologies.title: Extend Terminologies
extend_terminologies.description: Merge only — add terms the target's terminology is missing, and the names a term has in the archive but not on the target. Separate from add_missing on purpose: allowing new vocabulary entries is not the same decision as allowing new schemas.

align_templates.title: Align Templates
align_templates.description: Merge only — match templates by value instead of by version number: each archive template version maps onto the target version whose schema can take its documents, documents are re-pinned to it, and documents no target version can take are listed and not merged. For an archive from another install, whose version numbers do not line up with the target's; refused for a template both sides share.

carry_retirements.title: Carry Retirements
carry_retirements.description: Merge only — retire the target's active terms that the archive has retired, with the archive's reason and replacement. Without it they stay active and are reported as kept: deprecating a live term is a change to the target's definitions, which a merge makes only when asked to.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: Run every precondition (archive format, empty targets, reporting schema) and report what would be restored, without writing anything.

drop_stale_reporting.title: Drop Stale Reporting
drop_stale_reporting.description: When the target namespace's reporting schema already holds tables (stale data that would shadow the restore), drop it before restoring. Without this flag such a restore refuses.

allow_missing_identity.title: Allow Missing Identity
allow_missing_identity.description: Restore only — proceed even when the archive carries entity rows but no registry identity rows (e.g. a CLI export made with --skip-synonyms). Without this flag such a restore refuses, because the restored namespace would fail every id-based read while looking healthy on list surfaces.

drop_unresolved_edges.title: Drop Unresolved Edges
drop_unresolved_edges.description: Drop edge documents (templates with usage 'relationship') whose source_ref or target_ref points at a document that is neither in the archive nor on this install. They are not restored, with all their versions, and the job result and the restore provenance list each one. Without it they are restored with the archived id. Plain reference fields always keep their value; references that do not resolve are listed either way. A merge refuses unresolved references, so for a merge this is what lets such edges be left out.

allow_failed_verify.title: Allow Failed Verify
allow_failed_verify.description: Restore an archive whose own verification failed. An archive written by an archive transform records the transform's verify result in its derived_from chain; when the newest step's verdict is 'fail', the archive is known to be broken and every restore mode (restore, merge, fresh, dry runs included) refuses it unless this is set. Then the restore proceeds with a warning, and the restore provenance records accepted_failed_verify. Other derived archives restore with a warning either way.

allowed_templates.title: Allowed Templates
allowed_templates.description: Comma-separated templates (value, NS:VALUE, id or synonym), stored as ids

custom.title: Custom
custom.description: Custom metadata fields as a JSON object

template_id.title: Template Id
template_id.description: Template ID to validate all items against

template_version.title: Template Version
template_version.description: Specific template version to validate against (default: latest)

items.title: Items
items.description: Document data payloads to validate, each shaped like the singular validate `data`; at most 1000

BulkValidationRequest.title: BulkValidationRequest
BulkValidationRequest.description:
Request to validate multiple documents against ONE template.

Single-template-per-call: every item validates against the same
`template_id` in the same `namespace`. The dry-run validator has no write
path, so this is side-effect-free — no documents, versions, or
identity-hash registrations are created. Mirrors the singular
``ValidationRequest`` but takes a list of ``data`` payloads.

results.title: Results
results.description: One ValidationResponse per input item, in the same order

BulkValidationResponse.title: BulkValidationResponse
BulkValidationResponse.description:
Per-item validation results, in input order.

Each element is a full ``ValidationResponse`` — a document being invalid is
reported via that item's ``valid: false`` + ``errors``, not as a batch-level
error. An unresolvable template fails the whole request at the endpoint
(404), since the batch is single-template.

document_id.title: Document Id
document_id.description: Set for sampled documents; None for explicit payloads

CandidateValidationItem.title: CandidateValidationItem
CandidateValidationItem.description: One document's result against the candidate definition.

template_definition.title: Template Definition
template_definition.description: The candidate template definition (same shape as a create request: fields, identity_fields, rules, ...). Reference values should be canonical IDs or resolvable synonyms.

documents.title: Documents
documents.description: Explicit data payloads to validate (mutually exclusive with sample_template_id); at most 1000

sample_template_id.title: Sample Template Id
sample_template_id.description: Existing template whose most recently updated active documents are sampled

sample_limit.title: Sample Limit
sample_limit.description: Sample size when sample_template_id is used

CandidateValidationRequest.title: CandidateValidationRequest
CandidateValidationRequest.description:
Validate documents against an INLINE candidate template definition.

The what-if dry-run for schema evolution: nothing is created, cached, or
registered — the candidate exists only for this call. Provide EITHER
explicit ``documents`` payloads OR ``sample_template_id`` to validate the
most recently updated active documents of an existing template.

CandidateValidationResponse.title: CandidateValidationResponse
CandidateValidationResponse.description: Aggregate + per-document results of a candidate dry-run.

version.title: Version
version.description: Specific version to hard-delete (default: all versions). Ignored for soft-delete.

force.title: Force
force.description: Delete even if referenced: on file deletion, and on document deletion with hard_delete=true (without hard_delete, rejected with error_code=force_unsupported)

DeleteItem.title: DeleteItem
DeleteItem.description: Item in a bulk delete request.

error_code.title: Error Code
error_code.description: Machine-readable error code. Documented codes: not_found, forbidden, archived, identity_field_change, concurrency_conflict, validation_failed, reference_violation, internal_error, already_exists, incompatible_config, force_unsupported, invalid_names, name_collision, identity_fields_immutable, immutable_property, cross_namespace_reference, invalid_state, invalid_request, registry_error, synonym_conflict, registry_entry_not_removed, cross_namespace_relationship, archived_relationship_endpoint.

details.title: Details
details.description: Structured details, e.g. the compatibility diff for on_conflict=validate or, on an error, the rule that failed (details.rule).

template_version.title: Template Version
template_version.description: Template version the written (or unchanged) document is pinned to; on a migrate dry run, the version it would be pinned to.

template_version.title: Template Version
template_version.description: Specific template version to validate against (default: latest)

document_id.title: Document Id
document_id.description: With version: the pre-assigned document ID of a restore or migration, which the Registry uses as-is. Without version: the document this write updates — it must be the one the identity resolves to, or the item is refused (invalid_request, details.rule document_id_mismatch).

version.title: Version
version.description: Pre-assigned version (for restore/migration — skips Registry and version computation when used with document_id)

created_by.title: Created By
created_by.description: User or system creating this document

synonyms.title: Synonyms
synonyms.description: Optional synonym composite keys to register for this document in the Registry

on_synonym_conflict.title: On Synonym Conflict
on_synonym_conflict.description: How to handle an inline synonym that the Registry refuses (e.g. already owned by a different entry). 'fail' (default): the whole create fails, the document is NOT created, and any synonyms/entry allocated for it are rolled back — use this when the synonyms are load-bearing (e.g. you rely on original IDs to resolve after import). 'warn': the document is created and the refused synonyms are reported in `warnings`. A Registry that cannot answer (unreachable or an error status) is not a refusal: the create fails with registry_error in either mode.

DocumentCreateRequest.title: DocumentCreateRequest
DocumentCreateRequest.description: Request to create or update a document.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page (MongoDB _id of its last item), in cursor mode (start it with cursor=start). Null on the last page and in offset pagination.

DocumentListResponse.title: DocumentListResponse
DocumentListResponse.description: Response containing a list of documents.

template_id.title: Template Id
template_id.description: Template to migrate (canonical UUID or registered value/synonym)

from_version.title: From Version
from_version.description: Source template version the documents are currently pinned to. May be inactive (frozen) — migration validates against the target, not the source.

to_version.title: To Version
to_version.description: Target template version to re-pin to. Must be active.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: When true (default), report per-document readiness without writing. A dry-run with failed==0 guarantees a successful apply (barring concurrent writes).

DocumentMigrateRequest.title: DocumentMigrateRequest
DocumentMigrateRequest.description:
Request to migrate a cohort of documents from one template version to another.

Re-pins every active document currently on ``from_version`` to ``to_version``,
creating a new document version (or overwriting in place for ``versioned: false``
templates). The migration is **identity-preserving only**: the two template
versions must declare the same ``identity_fields``. If they differ the identity
hash would change — that is a *fork* (create new documents), not a migrate, and
the operation is rejected. The only data transformation applied is field renames
declared on the target template version (mechanical re-keying to the new field
names); any other per-document data prep (e.g. PATCH-null a removed field) is the
app's job, done while the source version is still writable.

DocumentMigrateResponse.title: DocumentMigrateResponse
DocumentMigrateResponse.description:
Bulk-first migrate result. Always HTTP 200; per-document outcome in ``results``.

Per-item status:
- ``updated`` — a new version was (apply) or would be (dry_run) pinned to to_version.
- ``error`` — the document fails validation against to_version (e.g. a now-removed
  field still present → ``unknown_field``, or a newly-mandatory field missing).
  ``error_code`` is ``validation_failed`` (details carry the field errors) or
  ``identity_hash_stale`` (the stored identity hash is not the one the
  document's identity produces under to_version; details carry both).

When ``dry_run`` is true the statuses are PROJECTED — nothing was written.

status.description: Filter by status (defaults to 'active' — pass null to include all versions)

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: Token to send as if_match on a PATCH of this document; equal to version except on a row overwritten in place (versioned:false), where it counts the writes

term_references.title: Term References
term_references.description: Resolved term IDs for term fields (legacy)

references.title: References
references.description: Resolved references for reference type fields

file_references.title: File References
file_references.description: Resolved file references for file fields

is_latest_version.title: Is Latest Version
is_latest_version.description: Whether this is the latest version of the document

latest_version.title: Latest Version
latest_version.description: The latest version number for this document_id

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: Token to send as if_match on a PATCH of this document, when this is its active version; equal to version except on a row overwritten in place (versioned:false), where it counts the writes

DocumentVersionSummary.title: DocumentVersionSummary
DocumentVersionSummary.description:
Summary of a document version.

``created_at`` is the ENTITY's creation time and is therefore identical on
every row — it does not tell you when this particular version was written.
``updated_at`` does: it is the moment this version row was persisted, which
is what makes the history a usable audit trail.

FileDocumentRef.title: FileDocumentRef
FileDocumentRef.description: A document that references a file.

FileDocumentsResponse.title: FileDocumentsResponse
FileDocumentsResponse.description: Paginated list of documents referencing a file.

FileDownloadResponse.title: FileDownloadResponse
FileDownloadResponse.description: Response containing a pre-signed download URL.

status.title: Status
status.description: healthy, warning, error, or incomplete — incomplete when some stored objects could not be checked and nothing worse was found

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: Count of issues by type, and how much of the object store was checked: storage_checked, storage_check_failed, storage_not_checked

FileListResponse.title: FileListResponse
FileListResponse.description: Response containing a list of files.

status.title: Status
status.description: Overall status: error or warning by the worst issue; incomplete when some checks could not run (summary.checks_not_run) and nothing was found; healthy only when every check ran

type.title: Type
type.description: Issue type: orphaned_template_ref, inactive_template_ref, orphaned_term_ref, orphaned_document_ref, misplaced_document_ref, orphaned_file_ref, identity_hash_mismatch, identity_field_missing, identity_resolution_missing, template_version_not_found, mandatory_field_missing, nested_template_not_found

identity_hash_mismatches.title: Identity Hash Mismatches
identity_hash_mismatches.description: Documents whose stored identity hash differs from the one recomputed

identity_unverified.title: Identity Unverified
identity_unverified.description: Documents whose identity could not be compared: an identity value or resolution missing, or the template version they are pinned to not found

mandatory_fields_missing.title: Mandatory Fields Missing
mandatory_fields_missing.description: Mandatory fields with no value in a document's current version: one per field, so a document can count more than once. Such a document is refused by its next PATCH

nested_templates_not_found.title: Nested Templates Not Found
nested_templates_not_found.description: Nested objects or array items whose pinned template version was not found, so their mandatory fields could not be checked

checks_not_run.title: Checks Not Run
checks_not_run.description: Checks skipped because a service could not answer, counted by '<check>:<service>' (e.g. 'term_reference:def-store'). Any count makes the status incomplete: an unchecked reference is not a healthy one.

keys.title: Keys
keys.description: The synonyms released, reclaimed, or held by another entry.

LifecycleItemResponse.title: LifecycleItemResponse
LifecycleItemResponse.description: One document the pass changed, or could not handle.

document_id.title: Document Id
document_id.description: Stable document ID (canonical UUID or registered synonym)

patch.title: Patch
patch.description: Partial data following RFC 7396 (JSON Merge Patch). Objects are deep-merged, arrays are replaced, null deletes a field. Pass {} for a metadata-only patch.

metadata_patch.title: Metadata Patch
metadata_patch.description: Partial metadata.custom following RFC 7396 (JSON Merge Patch), merged onto the document's custom metadata. Platform-owned metadata (warnings, source_system) cannot be addressed. A metadata change creates a new version like any other change.

if_match.title: If Match
if_match.description: Expected current revision (the document's `revision`, which equals its version except on a versioned:false template, where every in-place write moves it on). If provided and the document's revision differs, the item fails with concurrency_conflict.

PatchDocumentItem.title: PatchDocumentItem
PatchDocumentItem.description:
Item in a bulk PATCH /documents request.

Applies a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) to the document's `data` (and,
via `metadata_patch`, to `metadata.custom`) and creates a new version.
Metadata is non-identity document content: it versions like data but
never feeds the identity hash. Identity fields and namespace cannot be
changed via patch.

data.title: Data
data.description: Projected data fields from the peer doc — populated per the peer template's header_fields (or identity_fields fallback).

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Projected metadata fields. Only populated when the peer template's header_fields references metadata.custom.<name> paths.

PeerProjection.title: PeerProjection
PeerProjection.description:
Compact projection of a peer entity document for ?include=peers.

The relationships endpoint returns edge documents (relationship templates).
When ?include=peers is set, each item gains a peer field carrying the
entity at the OTHER end of the edge — direction-agnostic, latest active
version, projected down to the at-a-glance fields needed to render a
relationship sidebar without an N+1 fetch.

Field set is determined by the peer template's `header_fields`
declaration, falling back to `identity_fields`, and finally
to {title, doc_status} for templates with neither. `header_fields`
may reference data paths (bare names → data.<name>) or audit paths
(metadata.custom.<name>), so both `data` and `metadata` are surfaced
on the projection.

field.title: Field
field.description: Field path to filter on (e.g., 'data.status', 'template_id'). No segment may start with '$'.

operator.title: Operator
operator.description: Comparison operator: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, nin, exists, regex

value.title: Value
value.description: Value to compare against. An object or list may not contain a key starting with '$'.

QueryFilter.title: QueryFilter
QueryFilter.description:
A filter condition for document queries.

The field path is free: any ``data.<path>`` or document attribute, declared
on a template or not. What it cannot be is a MongoDB operator. A segment
starting with ``$`` (``$where``, ``$expr``, ``data.$x``) would put an
operator, and with ``$expr`` and ``$function`` server-side JavaScript,
where a field path goes. A value cannot carry operators either: ``operator`` names the only
comparison applied, so a ``$``-prefixed key anywhere in the value is
refused. A plain object value (``{"city": "Berlin"}``) still matches a
sub-document exactly.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the soft-deleted file to bring back (canonical id or synonym)

ReactivateFileItem.title: ReactivateFileItem
ReactivateFileItem.description: Item in a bulk file-reactivate request.

revive.title: Revive
revive.description: Also reclaim the released synonyms of every active document (a revival whose Registry call failed). Applied only, never on a dry run.

ReconcileSynonymLifecycleRequest.title: ReconcileSynonymLifecycleRequest
ReconcileSynonymLifecycleRequest.description: One pass aligning the Registry's synonym state with documents' lifecycle.

items.title: Items
items.description: Every document except the unchanged ones.

ReconcileSynonymLifecycleResponse.title: ReconcileSynonymLifecycleResponse
ReconcileSynonymLifecycleResponse.description: The pass report. A dry run and an apply return the same shape.

RehashCollisionGroup.title: RehashCollisionGroup
RehashCollisionGroup.description: Documents that converge on one (template, identity hash).

RehashIdentitiesRequest.title: RehashIdentitiesRequest
RehashIdentitiesRequest.description: One explicit identity-hash migration pass over a namespace.

applied.title: Applied
applied.description: Documents migrated completely: version rows rewritten AND the Registry re-key succeeded. 0 on a dry run.

registry_failed.title: Registry Failed
registry_failed.description: Documents whose Registry re-key did not succeed, whether their rows were rewritten by this run or by an earlier one. Re-run the apply once the cause is fixed: every apply re-sends the re-key for documents whose stored hash is already right. 0 on a dry run.

registry_repaired.title: Registry Repaired
registry_repaired.description: Documents whose stored hash was already right but whose Registry claim was not, re-keyed by this run (an earlier apply's Registry leg had failed). 0 on a dry run.

items.title: Items
items.description: Every scanned document except the unchanged ones; on an apply, also unchanged documents whose Registry re-key did not answer unchanged.

RehashIdentitiesResponse.title: RehashIdentitiesResponse
RehashIdentitiesResponse.description: The pass report. A dry run and an apply return the same shape.

status.title: Status
status.description: changed: the hash differs and the pass can apply it; unchanged: the stored hash is already right, listed only on an apply whose Registry re-key for it did not answer unchanged (see registry_status); unresolved: no stored resolution to recompute from, left as is; collision: another document converges on the same identity, reported and never applied; error: the template version was unreadable.

versions_updated.title: Versions Updated
versions_updated.description: Version rows rewritten; 0 on a dry run.

registry_status.title: Registry Status
registry_status.description: Outcome of the Registry re-key for this document: rekeyed or unchanged on success; not_found, conflict, error, missing or 'error: <reason>' otherwise. Null on a dry run and for documents the pass did not re-key.

RehashItemResponse.title: RehashItemResponse
RehashItemResponse.description: One document the pass did not leave unchanged.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: Token to send as if_match on a PATCH of this document; equal to version except on a row overwritten in place (versioned:false), where it counts the writes

term_references.title: Term References
term_references.description: Resolved term IDs for term fields (legacy)

references.title: References
references.description: Resolved references for reference type fields

file_references.title: File References
file_references.description: Resolved file references for file fields

is_latest_version.title: Is Latest Version
is_latest_version.description: Whether this is the latest version of the document

latest_version.title: Latest Version
latest_version.description: The latest version number for this document_id

peer_error_code.title: Peer Error Code
peer_error_code.description: Set when peer is null: not_found (missing, or in a namespace the caller cannot read).

RelationshipItem.title: RelationshipItem
RelationshipItem.description:
Edge document with optional peer projection.

When the caller passes ?include=peers, each item carries either:
  - peer: a PeerProjection of the entity at the OTHER end of the edge
  - peer_error_code: 'not_found' (peer is None) — also for a peer in a
    namespace the caller cannot read, which reports like a missing one

Inactive peers per PoNIF #1 are NOT errors — they are returned as a
populated peer object with status: 'inactive' so the UI can render them
dimmed. peer_error_code is reserved for actual resolution failures.

RelationshipListResponse.title: RelationshipListResponse
RelationshipListResponse.description:
Response shape for GET /documents/{id}/relationships.

Backwards-compatible with the prior DocumentListResponse: when
?include=peers is absent, items have no peer/peer_error_code/peer_error
fields populated and the shape is functionally identical.

ReplayFilter.title: ReplayFilter
ReplayFilter.description: Filter for replay — which documents to replay.

ReplayRequest.title: ReplayRequest
ReplayRequest.description: Request to start a replay session.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Namespace whose documents this session replays

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: 'restore' requires an empty target and inserts everything; 'merge' takes the archive as a delta against an existing, possibly non-empty namespace.

on_clash.title: On Clash
on_clash.description: Merge only — what to do when the target already holds a document's identity. 'skip' keeps the target's; 'overwrite' appends the archive's latest version on top of it; 'newer' does so only when the archive's copy was updated more recently.

older_versions.title: Older Versions
older_versions.description: Merge only — when 'overwrite' or 'newer' appends the archive's version on top of the target's, what happens to the target's older versions. 'retire' (default) soft-deletes them, as a normal write does; 'keep' leaves them active, so the document has several active versions.

add_missing.title: Add Missing
add_missing.description: Merge only — insert terminologies and templates the target does not have, instead of refusing.

extend_terminologies.title: Extend Terminologies
extend_terminologies.description: Merge only — add terms the target's terminology is missing, and the names a term has in the archive but not on the target.

align_templates.title: Align Templates
align_templates.description: Merge only — match templates by value instead of by version number: each archive template version maps onto the target version whose schema can take its documents, documents are re-pinned to it, and documents no target version can take are listed and not merged. For an archive from another install, whose version numbers do not line up with the target's; refused for a template both sides share.

carry_retirements.title: Carry Retirements
carry_retirements.description: Merge only — retire the target's active terms that the archive has retired, with the archive's reason and replacement. Without it they stay active and are reported as kept.

skip_documents.title: Skip Documents
skip_documents.description: Skip documents: neither their rows nor their Registry entries are restored

skip_files.title: Skip Files
skip_files.description: Skip files: neither their records, their blobs nor their Registry entries are restored

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: Run the preconditions and report what would happen without writing anything.

drop_stale_reporting.title: Drop Stale Reporting
drop_stale_reporting.description: mode='restore' only. When the target namespace's reporting schema already holds tables (stale data that would shadow the restore), drop it before restoring. Without this flag such a restore refuses.

drop_unresolved_edges.title: Drop Unresolved Edges
drop_unresolved_edges.description: Drop edge documents (templates with usage 'relationship') whose source_ref or target_ref points at a document that is neither in the archive nor on this install. They are not restored, with all their versions, and the job result and the restore provenance list each one. Without it they are restored with the archived id. Plain reference fields always keep their value; references that do not resolve are listed either way. A merge refuses unresolved references, so for a merge this is what lets such edges be left out.

allow_failed_verify.title: Allow Failed Verify
allow_failed_verify.description: Restore an archive whose own verification failed. When the newest step of the archive's derived_from chain records verdict 'fail', the restore (dry runs included) refuses unless this is set; then it proceeds with a warning and the restore provenance records accepted_failed_verify.

allow_missing_identity.title: Allow Missing Identity
allow_missing_identity.description: Restore only — proceed even when the archive carries entity rows but no registry identity rows (e.g. a CLI export made with --skip-synonyms). Without it such a restore refuses, because the restored namespace would fail every id-based read while looking healthy on list surfaces. Rejected for a merge.

RestoreFromJobRequest.title: RestoreFromJobRequest
RestoreFromJobRequest.description:
Request body for POST /backup/jobs/{job_id}/restore.

Unlike the upload restore (multipart form), this endpoint takes JSON —
the archive is already retained server-side, so there is no file part.
This model IS wired to the route, so its bounds are enforced.

RestoreProvenanceItem.title: RestoreProvenanceItem
RestoreProvenanceItem.description: A provenance record as the API serves it.

RestoreProvenanceListResponse.title: RestoreProvenanceListResponse
RestoreProvenanceListResponse.description: A namespace's restore history, oldest first.

storage_keys.title: Storage Keys
storage_keys.description: Storage keys recorded in the namespace's deletion journal

StorageDeleteRequest.title: StorageDeleteRequest
StorageDeleteRequest.description: Stored objects to remove for a namespace that is being deleted.

is_array.title: Is Array
is_array.description: Whether this is an array field

TableColumn.title: TableColumn
TableColumn.description: Metadata about a column in the table view.

total_documents.title: Total Documents
total_documents.description: Number of documents (their latest versions) matching the filter, across all pages, before flattening

total_rows.title: Total Rows
total_rows.description: Rows on this page after flattening

array_handling.title: Array Handling
array_handling.description: How arrays were handled on this page: 'flattened', 'json' (at least one document's arrays exceeded max_cross_product), or 'none' (no arrays on this page)

template_value.title: Template Value
template_value.description: Denormalized template value carried on the counted documents

template_namespace.title: Template Namespace
template_namespace.description: The template's OWN namespace — may differ from the queried namespace (shared / cross-namespace templates). None when the template could not be fetched.

document_count.title: Document Count
document_count.description: Distinct logical documents (version rows collapse on document_id before counting) of this template in the queried namespace

TemplateFacet.title: TemplateFacet
TemplateFacet.description: One template referenced by a namespace's documents, with its live count.

TemplateFacetsResponse.title: TemplateFacetsResponse
TemplateFacetsResponse.description:
Answer to: which templates are namespace X's documents instances of?

A document's namespace is independent of its template's namespace, so
listing the templates a namespace OWNS cannot answer this — a namespace
whose documents sit on shared or foreign templates would look empty.
These facets are grouped from the documents themselves, so every
reachable template appears, labeled with its true namespace.

total_live_docs.title: Total Live Docs
total_live_docs.description: Active rows on the template: one per document, except a document a restore kept with several active versions, counted per row

docs_per_version.title: Docs Per Version
docs_per_version.description: Active-document count per template_version (keys are stringified version numbers)

field_nonempty_counts.title: Field Nonempty Counts
field_nonempty_counts.description: Per requested field: active documents with a non-empty data.<field> (exists, not null, not empty string)

TemplateImpactStatsResponse.title: TemplateImpactStatsResponse
TemplateImpactStatsResponse.description:
Live-document counts for template version-change impact analysis.

Advisory read-only data: how many active documents each template version
carries, and — for each requested field — how many active documents hold
a non-empty value there. Consumed by the template create-as-upsert to
report the consequences of a version event; a field with zero non-empty
documents is safely droppable via migration.

depth.title: Depth
depth.description: Hops from the seed (1 = a direct neighbour)

via_relationship.title: Via Relationship
via_relationship.description: document_id of the relationship document that was traversed to reach this node (None for the seed).

path.title: Path
path.description: Chain of document_ids from seed (exclusive) to this node (inclusive).

TraverseNode.title: TraverseNode
TraverseNode.description:
One node in a relationship traversal result.

Each node is a document discovered during BFS expansion from the
starting document. `depth` is the number of relationship-document
hops away from the start, 1 for a direct neighbour; the start itself
is not listed.
`path` is the chain of document_ids visited to reach this node,
starting from the seed doc and excluding it (so a depth-1 node has
a 1-element path containing only itself).

types_filter.title: Types Filter
types_filter.description: Relationship template values used to constrain traversal; empty = all relationship templates.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: True if a depth-cap or expansion-cap stopped traversal before exhausting reachable nodes.

custom.title: Custom
custom.description: Additional custom metadata fields (merges with existing)

allowed_templates.title: Allowed Templates
allowed_templates.description: Templates whose documents may use this file, named as on upload and stored as canonical template ids. An empty list removes the restriction; omit the field to leave it unchanged.

UpdateFileItem.title: UpdateFileItem
UpdateFileItem.description: Item in a bulk file metadata update request — includes the ID.
